questions.question:
Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets.

(NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 - Operations on 13 such as adding/deleting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)

(31, 4, 47)

(17, 8, 81)
questions.solution:
**Given,**

**(31, 4, 47)**

**(17, 8, 81)**

Here, the following logic is used 

**(First number + (Second number)²) = Third number**

First Pair

(31, 4, 47)

(31 + 16) = 47

Second Pair

(17, 8, 81)

(17 + 64) = 81

Let's check every option one by one

**Option(1)**

(92) =30 (which is not possible)

**⇒ LHS ≠ RHS **

**Option(2)**

(19 + 25) = 44

44 = 44

**⇒ LHS = RHS **

**Option(3)**

(19, 11, 41)

(19 + 121 ) = 41

140 = 41 (which is not possible)

**⇒ LHS ≠ RHS **

**Option(4)**

(2, 12, 16)

(2 + 144) = 16

(146) = 16 (which is not possible)

**⇒ LHS ≠ RHS **

Only** ****(19, 5, 44)** follow the given logic.

questions.question: In a certain code language, 'TEA' is coded as 78, and 'SHAKE' is coded as 220. How will 'COFFEE' be coded in that language?
questions.solution:
The position of the letters according to the English alphabet series:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/95e8d7f18fcf2b6801af6bc9d1c6a9b0f0dbfacea23a7bd8da0f6df6b5ef99f5.png] 

The logic here follows is:

__**Adding all the positional values of the given letters, and multiplying by the number of letters.**__

 
• In the word, 'TEA' the number of letters are '**3**'. **T⇒20, E⇒5, A⇒1**

 TEA = (20 + 5 + 1) × 3

 TEA = 26 × 3

 **TEA = 78**

 
• In the same way, the word 'SHAKE' has number of letters '**5**'. **S⇒19, H⇒8, A⇒1, K⇒11, E⇒5**

** **SHAKE = (19 + 8 + 1 + 11 + 5) × 5

 SHAKE = 44 × 5

 **SHAKE = 220**

 
• Similarly, in the word 'COFFEE' the number of letters are '**6**'. **C⇒3, O⇒15, F⇒6, E⇒5**

** **COFFEE = (3 + 15 + 6 + 6 + 5 + 5) × 6

 COFFEE = 40 × 6 

 **COFFEE = 240**

Hence, the correct answer is '**240.'**

questions.question:
In this question, three statements are given, followed by two conclusions numbered I, II. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusion(s) logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements**:

All cakes are pastries. 

Some pastries are chocolates. 

All chocolates are biscuits.

**Conclusions**:

I. Some biscuits are pastries. 

II. All cakes are chocolates

options.text: Both conclusions I and II follow.
Neither conclusion I nor II follows.

questions.solution:
Given,

Statements:

All cakes are pastries. 

Some pastries are chocolates. 

All chocolates are biscuits.

__**Venn Diagram**__:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c7a31d23eac4a3ceac17bd9825f48f2a017d2469ec9d43c9fc9768b06af70647.png] 

__**Conclusions**__**:**

I. Some biscuits are pastries. →**True**(All chocolates are biscuits, and some chocolates are pastries.) 

II. All cakes are chocolates → **False **(No definite relation.)

Hence, the correct answer is "__**Only conclusion I follows.**__"

questions.question: In a code language, 'ROSE' is coded as 228 and 'TULIP' is coded as 390. How will 'DAHLIA' be coded in the same language?
questions.solution:
The position of the letters according to the English alphabet series:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/95e8d7f18fcf2b6801af6bc9d1c6a9b0f0dbfacea23a7bd8da0f6df6b5ef99f5.png] 

__
 
• The logic follows here is:

 **Adding all the positional value of the respective letters and then multiplying the sum by the number of letters present in the word.**__

 
• In the word **"ROSE"**,** **the number of letters '**4'. R⇒18, O⇒15, S⇒19, E⇒5**

** **ROSE =** **(18 + 15 + 19 + 5) × 4

 ROSE = 57 × 4** **

** ROSE = 228.**

 
• In the same way, **"TULIP"**, the number of letters '**5**'. **T⇒20, U⇒21, L⇒12, I⇒9, P⇒16**

 TULIP = (20 + 21 + 12 + 9 + 16) × 5

 TULIP = 78 × 5

 **TULIP = 390**

 
• Similarly, in the word **"DAHLIA"**, the number of letters '**6**'. **D⇒4, A⇒1, H⇒8, L⇒12, I⇒9, A⇒1**

** **DAHLIA = (4 + 1 + 8 + 12 + 9 + 1) × 6

 DAHLIA = 35 × 6

 **DAHLIA = 210**

Hence, the correct answer is **"210".**

questions.question:
In this question, three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusion(s) logically follow(s) from the statements..

**Statements: **

Some mugs are jars.

All jars are bottles.

All glasses are mugs.

**Conclusions: **

I. All glasses are jars.

II. Some glasses are bottles.

III. Some mugs are bottles

options.text: Only conclusion II and III follows.
Only conclusion I and III follows.

questions.solution:
Given,

Statements:

Some mugs are jars.

All jars are bottles.

All glasses are mugs.

**__Venn Diagram__**:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e9cd3bcc885e66cd98830bdba53c8c20d77d7679e94a512be6ecdba0965e1829.png] 

Conclusions:

I. All glasses are jars. → **False **(Can be true, but not definite)

I. Some glasses are bottles. → **False **(Can be true, but not definite.)

III. Some mugs are bottles. → **True **(Definite relation ⇒ All jars are **bottles**, and some **mugs** are jars)

Hence, the correct answer is '**only conclusions III follows.**'

questions.question:
Two dimensions of the same dice are given. What letter will be on the face opposite to the face having the letter E?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9af9a74bc48f9d842bf44cf471acdccbac4dc98002c195a6de92615468b60694.png]
questions.solution:
According to the given figures,

C is the common face in both dice.

The adjacent letter of C is A, E, F, D

No adjacent surface can be the opposite faces.

So, B is the opposite face of C.

While comparing both the surfaces :

'A' is the opposite of 'F' and 'E' is the opposite of 'D'

 '**E**' will appear on the face opposite of '**D**'

Hence, the correct answer is '**D**'
